questions.stem: The longest wavelength associated with Paschen series is : (Given $R_{H} = 1.097 \times 10^{7}$ SI unit)
questions.solution:
For longest wavelength in Paschen's series:
$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left[\frac{1}{n_1^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_2^{2}}\right]$$
For longest $n_1 = 3$, $n_2 = 4$
$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left[\frac{1}{(3)^{2}} - \frac{1}{(4)^{2}}\right]$$
$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left[\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{16}\right]$$
$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left[\frac{16-9}{16 \times 9}\right]$$
$$\Rightarrow \lambda = \frac{16 \times 9}{7R} = \frac{16 \times 9}{7 \times 1.097 \times 10^{7}}$$
$\lambda = 1.876 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m}$

questions.stem: A total of 48 J heat is given to one mole of helium kept in a cylinder. The temperature of helium increases by $2^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The work done by the gas is : (Given, $R = 8.3\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}mol^{-1}}$.)
questions.solution:
$1^{\mathrm{st}}$ law of thermodynamics
$\Delta Q = \Delta U + W$
$\Rightarrow +48 = nC_v\Delta T + W$
$\Rightarrow 48 = (1)\left(\frac{3R}{2}\right)(2) + W$
$\Rightarrow W = 48 - 3 \times R$
$\Rightarrow W = 48 - 3 \times (8.3)$
$\Rightarrow W = 23.1\ \mathrm{Joule}$

questions.stem:
In finding out refractive index of glass slab the following observations were made through travelling microscope 50 vernier scale division = 49 MSD; 20 divisions on main scale in each cm
For mark on paper
$\mathrm{MSR} = 8.45\ \mathrm{cm}$, $\mathrm{VC} = 26$
For mark on paper seen through slab
$\mathrm{MSR} = 7.12\ \mathrm{cm}$, $\mathrm{VC} = 41$
For powder particle on the top surface of the glass slab
$\mathrm{MSR} = 4.05\ \mathrm{cm}$, $\mathrm{VC} = 1$
(MSR = Main Scale Reading, VC = Vernier Coincidence)
Refractive index of the glass slab is:
questions.solution:
$1\ \mathrm{MSD} = \frac{1\ \mathrm{cm}}{20} = 0.05\ \mathrm{cm}$
$1\ \mathrm{VSD} = \frac{49}{50}\mathrm{MSD} = \frac{49}{50} \times 0.05\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.049\ \mathrm{cm}$
$\mathrm{LC} = 1\mathrm{MSD} - 1\mathrm{VSD} = 0.001\ \mathrm{cm}$
For mark on paper, $L_1 = 8.45\ \mathrm{cm} + 26 \times 0.001\ \mathrm{cm} = 84.76\ \mathrm{mm}$
For mark on paper through slab, $L_2 = 7.12\ \mathrm{cm} + 41 \times 0.001\ \mathrm{cm} = 71.61\ \mathrm{mm}$
For powder particle on top surface, $\mathrm{ZE} = 4.05\ \mathrm{cm} + 1 \times 0.001\ \mathrm{cm} = 40.51\ \mathrm{mm}$
$\therefore$ actual $L_1 = 84.76 - 40.51 = 44.25\ \mathrm{mm}$
actual $L_2 = 71.61 - 40.51 = 31.10\ \mathrm{mm}$
$$L_2 = \frac{L_1}{\mu}$$
$$\Rightarrow \mu = \frac{L_1}{L_2} = \frac{44.25}{31.10} = 1.42$$

questions.stem:
In the given electromagnetic wave
$E_y = 600 \sin (\omega t - kx)\ \mathrm{Vm^{-1}}$, intensity of the associated light beam is (in $\mathrm{W/m^{2}}$): (Given $\epsilon_0 = 9 \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{C^{2}N^{-1}m^{-2}}$)
questions.solution:
$$\text{Intensity} = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E_0^{2} c$$
$$= \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 10^{-12} \times (600)^{2} \times 3 \times 10^{8}$$
$$= \frac{9}{2} \times 36 \times 3 = 486\ \mathrm{w/m^{2}}$$

questions.stem: Assuming the earth to be a sphere of uniform mass density, a body weighed 300 N on the surface of earth. How much it would weigh at R/4 depth under surface of earth ?
questions.solution:
At surface: $mg = 300\ \mathrm{N}$
$$m = \frac{300}{g_s}$$
At Depth $\frac{R}{4}$: $g_d = g_s\left[1 - \frac{d}{R}\right]$
$$g_d = g_s\left[1 - \frac{R}{4R}\right]$$
$$g_d = \frac{3g_s}{4}$$
weight at depth $= m \times g_d = m \times \frac{3g_s}{4} = \frac{3}{4} \times 300 = 225\ \mathrm{N}$

questions.stem: The acceptor level of a p-type semiconductor is 6 eV. The maximum wavelength of light which can create a hole would be : Given $hc = 1242\ \mathrm{eV\,nm}$
questions.solution:
Energy $= \frac{hc}{\lambda}$ ;
$$E = \frac{1240}{\lambda(\mathrm{nm})}\ \mathrm{eV}$$
$$6 = \frac{1240}{\lambda(\mathrm{nm})}$$
$$\lambda = \frac{1240}{6} = 207\ \mathrm{nm}$$

questions.stem: A car of 800 kg is taking turn on a banked road of radius 300 m and angle of banking $30^\circ$. If coefficient of static friction is 0.2 then the maximum speed with which car can negotiate the turn safely : ($g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$, $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)
questions.solution:
$m = 800\ \mathrm{kg}$
$r = 300\ \mathrm{m}$
$\theta = 30^\circ$
$\mu_s = 0.2$
$$V_{max} = \sqrt{Rg\left[\frac{\tan\theta + \mu}{1 - \mu\tan\theta}\right]}$$
$$= \sqrt{300 \times g \times \left[\frac{\tan 30^\circ + 0.2}{1 - 0.2 \times \tan 30^\circ}\right]}$$
$$= \sqrt{300 \times 10 \times \left[\frac{0.57 + 0.2}{1 - 0.2 \times 0.57}\right]}$$
$V_{max} = 51.4\ \mathrm{m/s}$

questions.stem: Two identical conducting spheres P and S with charge Q on each, repel each other with a force 16N. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere R is successively brought in contact with the two spheres. The new force of repulsion between P and S is :
questions.solution:
$F_{PS} \propto Q^{2}$
$F_{PS} = 16\ \mathrm{N}$
Now If P & R are brought in contact then
Now If S & R are brought in contact then
New force between P & S is :

questions.stem: In a coil, the current changes form $-2\ \mathrm{A}$ to $+2\mathrm{A}$ in 0.2 s and induces an emf of 0.1 V. The self-inductance of the coil is :
questions.solution:
$(\mathrm{Emf})_{induced} = -L\frac{di}{dt}$
In magnitude form,
$$\left|\mathrm{Emf}_{ind}\right| = \left|(-)L\frac{di}{dt}\right|$$
$$\Rightarrow 0.1 = \frac{(L)[+2-(-2)]}{0.2}$$
$$\Rightarrow L = \frac{0.1 \times 0.2}{4} = 5\ \mathrm{mH}$$

questions.stem: For the thin convex lens, the radii of curvature are at 15 cm and 30 cm respectively. The focal length the lens is 20 cm. The refractive index of the material is :
questions.solution:
$$\frac{1}{f} = \left(\frac{\mu_{lens}}{\mu_{air}} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{+20} = \left(\frac{\mu}{1} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{+15} - \frac{1}{(-30)}\right)$$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{20} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{3}{30}\right)$$
$$\Rightarrow \mu - 1 = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\Rightarrow \mu = 1 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5$$

questions.stem: Energy of 10 non rigid diatomic molecules at temperature T is :
questions.solution:
Degree of freedom$(f) = 5 + 2(3N - 5)$
$f = 5 + 2(3 \times 2 - 1) = 7$
energy of one molecule $= \frac{f}{2}K_BT$
energy of 10 molecules
$$= 10\left(\frac{f}{2}K_BT\right) = 10\left(\frac{7}{2}K_BT\right) = 35\ K_BT$$

questions.stem: When UV light of wavelength 300 nm is incident on the metal surface having work function 2.13 eV, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is : (Given $hc = 1240\ \mathrm{eV\,nm}$)
questions.solution:
$$\frac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi = e.V_s$$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{1240}{300}\ \mathrm{eV} - 2.13\ \mathrm{eV} = eV_s$$
$$\Rightarrow 4.13\ \mathrm{eV} - 2.13\ \mathrm{eV} = eV_s.$$
$$\Rightarrow \text{So, } V_s = 2\ \mathrm{volt}$$

questions.stem: The number of electrons flowing per second in the filament of a 110 W bulb operating at 220 V is : (Given $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$)
questions.solution:
Power $(P) = V.I$
$\Rightarrow 110 = (220)(I)$
$\Rightarrow I = 0.5\ \mathrm{A}$
Now, $I = \frac{n \cdot e}{t}$
$$\Rightarrow 0.5 = \left(\frac{n}{t}\right)(1.6 \times 10^{-19})$$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{n}{t} = \frac{0.5}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}}$$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{n}{t} = 31.25 \times 10^{17}$$

questions.stem: When kinetic energy of a body becomes 36 times of its original value, the percentage increase in the momentum of the body will be :
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy $(K) = \frac{P^{2}}{2m}$
$\Rightarrow P = \sqrt{2mK}$
If $K_f = 36\ K_i$
So, $P_f = 6\ P_i$
$$\%\text{ increase in momentum} = \frac{P_f - P_i}{P_i} \times 100\%$$
$$= \frac{6P_i - P_i}{P_i} \times 100\%$$
$$= 500\%$$

questions.stem:
Pressure inside a soap bubble is greater than the pressure outside by an amount :

questions.solution:
There are two liquid-air surfaces in bubble so
$$\Delta P = 2\left(\frac{2S}{R}\right) = \frac{4S}{R}$$

In Franck-Hertz experiment, the first dip in the current-voltage graph for hydrogen is observed at 10.2 V. The wavelength of light emitted by hydrogen atom when excited to the first excitation level is ______ nm.

questions.solution:

questions.stem: For a given series LCR circuit it is found that maximum current is drawn when value of variable capacitance is 2.5 nF. If resistance of $200\ \Omega$ and 100 mH inductor is being used in the given circuit. The frequency of ac source is _____ $\times 10^{3}$ Hz. (given $\pi^{2} = 10$)
questions.solution:
for maximum current, circuit must be in resonance.
$$f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{L \times C}}$$
$$f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{100 \times 10^{-3} \times 2.5 \times 10^{-9}}}$$
$$= \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{25 \times 10^{-11}}}$$
$$= \frac{1}{2\pi \times 5} \times 10^{5} \times \sqrt{10}\ \mathrm{Hz}$$
$$= \frac{100}{10} \times 10^{3}\ \mathrm{Hz}$$
$f_0 = 10 \times 10^{3}\ \mathrm{Hz}$

questions.stem: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement x at any time t is given by $x^{2} = 1 + t^{2}$. Its acceleration at any time t is $x^{-n}$ where n = _____.

Three balls of masses 2kg, 4kg and 6kg respectively are arranged at centre of the edges of an equilateral triangle of side 2 m. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis through the centroid and perpendicular to the plane of triangle, will be ______ $\mathrm{kg\ m^{2}}$.
questions.solution:
$r = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
Moment of inertia about C and perpendicular to the plane is :
$I = r^{2}\,[2 + 4 + 6]$
$= \frac{1}{3} \times 12$
$I = 4\ \mathrm{kg\text{-}m^{2}}$

questions.topic: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem: A coil having 100 turns, area of $5 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^{2}}$, carrying current of 1 mA is placed in uniform magnetic field of 0.20 T such a way that plane of coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The work done in turning the coil through $90^\circ$ is _____ $\mu\mathrm{J}$.
questions.solution:
$W = \Delta U = U_f - U_i$
$W = (-\vec{\mu}.\vec{B})_f - (-\vec{\mu}.\vec{B})_i$
$= 0 + (\vec{\mu}.\vec{B})_i$
$= (100 \times 5 \times 10^{-3} \times 1 \times 10^{-3}) \times 0.2\ \mathrm{J}$
$= 1 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{J} = 100\ \mu\mathrm{J}$

questions.stem: In the given figure an ammeter A consists of a $240\Omega$ coil connected in parallel to a $10\ \Omega$ shunt. The reading of the ammeter is ______ mA.
questions.solution:
$R_{eq} = 140.4 + \frac{240 \times 10}{240 + 10}$
$R_{eq} = 140.4 + \frac{2400}{250}$
$R_{eq.} = 150\Omega$
$\therefore$ Current in ammeter $= \frac{24}{150} = 160\ \mathrm{mA}$

questions.stem:
A wire of cross sectional area A, modulus of elasticity $2 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{Nm^{-2}}$ and length 2 m is stretched between two vertical rigid supports. When a mass of 2 kg is suspended at the middle it sags lower from its original position making angle $\theta = \frac{1}{100}$ radian on the points of support. The value of A is _____ $\times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^{2}}$ (consider $x \ll L$).
(given : $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution:
In vertical direction
$2T\sin\theta = 20$
using small angle approximation $\sin\theta = \theta$
$$\theta = \frac{1}{100}$$
$$\therefore T = \frac{10}{\theta}$$
$T = 1000\ \mathrm{N}$
Change in length $\Delta L = 2\sqrt{x^{2} + L^{2}} - 2L$
$$= 2L\left[1 + \frac{x^{2}}{2L^{2}} - 1\right]$$
$$\Delta L = \frac{x^{2}}{L}$$
$\therefore$ Modulus of elasticity $= \frac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}}$
$$2 \times 10^{11} = \frac{10^{3}}{A \times \frac{x^{2}}{L}} \times 2L$$
$\therefore A = 1 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^{2}}$

questions.stem: Two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities I and 4I are superimposed. The difference between maximum and minimum possible intensities in the resulting beam is x I. The value of x is______.
questions.solution:
$$I_{max} = \left(\sqrt{I} + \sqrt{4I}\right)^{2} = 9I$$
$$I_{min} = \left(\sqrt{4I} - \sqrt{I}\right)^{2} = I$$
$\therefore I_{max} - I_{min} = 8I$

questions.stem:
Two open organ pipes of length 60 cm and 90 cm resonate at $6^{\mathrm{th}}$ and $5^{\mathrm{th}}$ harmonics respectively. The difference of frequencies for the given modes is _____ Hz.
(Velocity of sound in air = 333 m/s)
questions.solution:
The difference in frequency in open organ pipe =
$$f = \frac{nv}{2L}$$
$$\Delta f = \frac{6v}{2 \times 0.6} - \frac{5v}{2 \times 0.9}$$
$v = 333\ \mathrm{m/s}$
$\Delta f = 740\ \mathrm{Hz}$
